trigger_phrase: heaven and earth
footnote_text: The Greek phrase can function as a totality expression, referring to the whole ordered world rather than only the sky above and the soil below. NETS, LES, and LES2 keep this heaven-and-earth pairing close to the Greek line.

trigger_phrase: the Spirit of God
footnote_text: Greek pneuma can mean wind, breath, or spirit, but in this creation context the line is best read as the Spirit of God rather than merely meteorological wind. Local Logos word-sense evidence supports that reading.

trigger_phrase: come to be
footnote_text: The Greek verb is from ginomai, which often signals becoming or coming into being. This draft keeps that verbal echo in both command and fulfillment.

trigger_phrase: day one
footnote_text: Greek uses a cardinal expression here, literally "day one," rather than the more expected ordinal "first day." English witnesses are split, and the draft keeps the Greek cardinal force visible rather than smoothing to an ordinal.

trigger_phrase: firm span
footnote_text: Greek stereoma points to something fixed or made firm. "Firm span" aims to preserve that sense without defaulting either to the older "firmament" or to a purely empty "expanse."

trigger_phrase: one gathering
footnote_text: Greek speaks of the waters being brought into "one gathering" and then into "their gatherings," keeping the image of collected water visible more strongly than the smoother phrase "one place."

trigger_phrase: gathered bodies of the waters
footnote_text: Greek literally refers to gathered formations or collected bodies of water. This draft keeps the fuller phrase visible rather than shortening it to gathered waters.

trigger_phrase: according to kind and according to likeness
footnote_text: The Greek command uses both "kind" and "likeness" with repeated according-to phrasing. The fruit-tree language is singular in Greek, and the Hebrew line is also singular/collective rather than plural.

trigger_phrase: according to kind and according to likeness
footnote_text: Verse 12 echoes the command in verse 11 with repeated according-to phrasing and singular fruit-tree language.

trigger_phrase: light-bearers
footnote_text: Greek does not simply say light as an abstract thing but uses a term for bodies that bear or give light. Hebrew meorot likewise means lights, luminaries, or light-giving bodies.

trigger_phrase: dominions
footnote_text: Greek uses plural archas, a noun from the beginning/rule family, for the day and night domains. Hebrew memshelet means rule or dominion and is singular here.

trigger_phrase: crawling things of living souls
footnote_text: Greek says crawling things of living souls, using psyche for soul. Hebrew nephesh chayyah likewise means living soul, living being, or living creature.

trigger_phrase: great sea-monsters
footnote_text: Greek kete is more vivid than a generic sea-creature term here, and Hebrew tanninim likewise means sea monsters or great sea creatures.

trigger_phrase: winged creatures be multiplied
footnote_text: Greek uses a passive imperative for the winged creatures: let them be multiplied upon the earth.

trigger_phrase: living soul
footnote_text: Greek says living soul, using psyche. Hebrew nephesh chayyah likewise means living soul, living being, or living creature.

trigger_phrase: cattle

trigger_phrase: image and likeness

trigger_phrase: man

trigger_phrase: the man
footnote_text: Greek uses singular the man and him before the line shifts to them in male and female he made them.

trigger_phrase: seed-bearing plant sowing seed
footnote_text: Greek repeats the seed/sowing vocabulary in the food-gift line; the wording keeps that repetition visible.

trigger_phrase: soul of life

trigger_phrase: very good
footnote_text: Greek adds an intensifier to the evaluation of all things as many as God made; English supplies they were for readability.

trigger_phrase: ordered array

footnote_text: The Greek here says God completed his works on the sixth day and rested on the seventh. The Hebrew Masoretic text reads seventh day in the first clause.

trigger_phrase: begun to make
footnote_text: The Greek closes with an unusual phrase, literally speaking of the works God began to make. Hebrew is smoother here without the began wording.

trigger_phrase: book of the genesis
footnote_text: Greek literally uses genesis-language here. Hebrew uses toledot language for generations account or origins.

trigger_phrase: spring

trigger_phrase: formed

trigger_phrase: living soul

trigger_phrase: garden
footnote_text: Greek paradeisos can denote a garden park or paradise. In this Eden setting garden keeps the immediate scene clear.

trigger_phrase: tree of knowing good and evil
footnote_text: Greek uses an unusual knowing known construction here. The main line keeps the readable sense while this note preserves the more complex syntax.

trigger_phrase: four heads
footnote_text: Greek speaks of the river dividing into four heads, a term used for source-points or chief branches. Hebrew also uses head-language here.

trigger_phrase: helper corresponding to him
footnote_text: Greek does not merely say helper but adds language of correspondence or counterpart. Hebrew likewise carries the sense of a helper corresponding to him.

trigger_phrase: trance

trigger_phrase: woman / man

trigger_phrase: lie in wait for your head

trigger_phrase: your turning
footnote_text: Greek uses a noun of turning or orientation here, not the later traditional wording desire. Hebrew is often read as desire or turning toward. This draft keeps the directional sense visible.

trigger_phrase: skin tunics
footnote_text: Greek and Hebrew both use concrete tunic or garment plus skin language. This draft avoids softer wording like clothes so the image stays stark and material.

trigger_phrase: persons
footnote_text: Greek says "souls," but here the phrase functions as a headcount of living persons descending from Jacob. This draft avoids importing later metaphysical overtones into a census line.

trigger_phrase: the land multiplied them
footnote_text: The final clause is strikingly active in Greek, literally "the land multiplied them." This draft keeps that rough force for now rather than smoothing it away too quickly.

trigger_phrase: deal shrewdly with them
footnote_text: Greek uses a wisdom-root verb here. Pharaoh proposes not open argument but calculated cunning against Israel.

trigger_phrase: made their life bitter
footnote_text: The Greek phrase frames oppression as embittering life itself, not merely assigning hard tasks. This draft keeps that emotional and bodily force.

trigger_phrase: established households for themselves
footnote_text: Greek literally speaks of making houses for themselves. In context the line likely points to settled households or families, not merely buildings.

trigger_phrase: basket
footnote_text: Greek uses an uncommon loanword here, not the ordinary word for boat or chest. "Basket" keeps the small, portable object in view while leaving room to explore intertextual echoes later.

trigger_phrase: drew him out of the water
footnote_text: The naming explanation turns on drawing up from water. This draft keeps the etymological play explicit even if the exact wordplay does not map neatly into English.

trigger_phrase: grown great
footnote_text: Greek may suggest more than simple aging. This draft keeps both maturity and emerging stature in view.

trigger_phrase: settled with the man
footnote_text: The Greek verb points to settled placement or establishment. This draft emphasizes Moses taking up durable residence rather than merely staying overnight.

trigger_phrase: was made known to them
footnote_text: Greek does not simply say that God knew them; it uses a passive form, literally "was made known to them." This draft keeps that striking formulation visible for review.

trigger_phrase: angel of the Lord
footnote_text: Greek angelos can mean messenger as well as angel, but this scene signals more than ordinary envoy language. Bush burns without being consumed, and figure appears in openly theophanic context, so draft uses angel here.

trigger_phrase: what is it

trigger_phrase: have surely visited you

trigger_phrase: has summoned us
footnote_text: The verb can mean call or summon. This draft stresses formal divine commissioning before Pharaoh.

trigger_phrase: except under a mighty hand

trigger_phrase: weak-voiced and slow-tongued

trigger_phrase: speechless and deaf

trigger_phrase: in the things toward God

trigger_phrase: God had visited
footnote_text: The same visitation language used earlier returns here. This draft preserves that verbal link between promise and fulfillment.

trigger_phrase: empty words

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: But let the weak perish in war, and let the powerless come out from the hand of the mighty.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And let there be hope for the powerless, but mouth of the unrighteous be stopped.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: But blessed is man whom the Lord corrected; do not reject discipline of the Almighty.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For he causes pain and again restores. He struck, and his hands healed.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Six times from necessities he will deliver you, and in the seventh evil will not touch you.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: In famine he will rescue you from death, and in war he will free you from the hand of iron.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: From scourge of the tongue he will hide you, and you will not fear evils coming.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: You will laugh at unjust and lawless men, and you will not fear from wild beasts,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: for wild beasts will be at peace with you.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Then you will know that your house will be at peace, and dwelling of your tent will never go wrong.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And you will know that your seed is many, and your children will be like all-herbage of the field.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And you will come to the grave like ripe grain harvested in its season, or like a heap of threshing floor gathered at its time.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Behold, these things we searched out. These are what we heard. But you, know for yourself if you did anything.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And taking up the matter, Iōb says,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If only someone might weigh my anger, and lift my pains together in balance.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seashore; but, as it seems, my words are worthless.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For arrows of the Lord are in my body, whose fury drinks up my blood; whenever I begin to speak, they stab me.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For surely wild donkey does not cry for nothing, unless seeking grain; nor will ox bellow at manger while having fodder.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Will bread be eaten without salt? Or is there taste in empty words?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For my soul cannot cease, for I see my foods as stench, like smell of lion.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If only my request might come, and the Lord might give my hope.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Let the Lord begin and wound me; but in end let him not destroy me.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Let my city be grave, upon whose walls I leaped; upon it I will by no means spare myself, for I did not lie about words of holy God.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For what strength have I, that I keep enduring? Or what time remains for me, that my soul keeps bearing?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Is my strength the strength of stones, or is my flesh bronze?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Or was I not trusting in him? But help has gone far from me.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Mercy renounced me, and visitation of the Lord overlooked me.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: My near ones did not regard me; like failing torrents, or like a wave they passed me by.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Those who feared me before have now fallen upon me, like snow or frozen ice.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: As things melted when heat came, what they were was not recognized.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Thus I too was abandoned by all; I perished and became homeless.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Look at ways of Thaimanites, paths of Sabaeans, those who look intently.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: They will owe shame, those trusting in cities and riches.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: But now you too fell upon me without mercy, so that seeing my wound you were afraid.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For what? Did I ask anything from you, or do I need some of your strength?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: So as to save me from enemies, or rescue me from the hand of rulers?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Teach me, and I will be silent; if I have gone astray, show me.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: As it seems, the words of truth are worthless, for I do not ask strength from you.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Nor will your reproof stop me with words, for neither will I endure the sound of your speech.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Only because you fall upon orphan, and spring against your friend.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: But now, looking into your faces, I will not lie.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Sit down then, and let there not be injustice; and again come together with righteous judgment.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For there is no injustice on my tongue; does not my throat ponder understanding?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Is not life of man on earth a trial, and his life like that of day-laborer?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Like servant fearing his master and having attained shade, like a hired man waiting for his wage,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: so I too inherited empty months, and nights of pains were given me.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If I lie down, I say, When day? and when I rise again, When evening? And I am full of pains from evening until morning.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: My body is mixed with rottenness of worms; I melt clods of earth, scraping off the discharge.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: My life is lighter than speech, and has perished in empty hope.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Remember then that my life is breath, and my eye will no longer return to see good.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Eye of one seeing me will not look on me; your eyes are on me, and I am no longer.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Like cloud cleansed away from heaven, if man goes down to Hades, he will certainly not come up again.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Nor will he ever return again to his own house, nor will his place know him anymore.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: But therefore neither will I spare my mouth; I will speak in distress, opening bitterness of my soul while hard pressed.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Am I sea or dragon, that you set a guard over me?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If I say, My bed will comfort me, and my couch will bear my complaint for me,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: then you frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: You will free my soul from breath, and my bones from death.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For I will not live forever, that I should be patient. Depart from me, for my life is empty.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: What is man, that you magnified him, or that you set your mind on him,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: or make visitation of him until morning, and judge him for rest?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Until when will you not let me be, nor release me until I swallow my spittle in pain?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If I sinned, what can I do to you, knower of minds of men? Why did you set me as your accuser? And I have become burden to you.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And why did you not make forgetfulness of my lawlessness and cleansing of my sin? For now I will depart into earth, and seeking me early, I am no more.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And taking up the matter, Baldad the Shuhite says,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: How long will you speak these things, wind of many words from your mouth?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Will the Lord do injustice in judging, or will maker of all disturb what is right?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If your sons sinned before him, he sent them away in the hand of their lawlessness.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: But you, rise early toward the Lord, begging Almighty.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If you are pure and true, he will hear your petition and restore to you dwelling of righteousness.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Then your first things will be few, but your last things beyond counting.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Ask indeed former generation, and search out race of fathers.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For we are of yesterday and do not know; for our life on earth is shadow.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Will not these teach you and tell you, and bring out words from their heart?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Does papyrus flourish without water, or will reed rise high without drink?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: While still on its root and not yet cut, before any herb drinks, does it not dry up?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: So then will be the end of all who forget the Lord, for the hope of the ungodly will perish.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For his house will be uninhabited, and his tent will turn out to be spider's web.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If he lean on his house, it will not stand; if he take hold of it, it will not endure.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For it is moist under the sun, and from its decay its shoot will come out.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: It sleeps upon gathering of stones, and in the midst of pebbles it will live.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If place swallow it up, it will deny it: You have not seen such things.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For such is overthrow of the ungodly, and from earth another will sprout.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For the Lord will by no means reject blameless one, but will not receive any gift of the ungodly.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Yet he will fill mouth of true ones with laughter, and their lips with confession.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: But their enemies will clothe themselves with shame, and the dwelling of the ungodly will not be.
footnote_text: Article cleanup: English supplies the before dwelling for readable subject syntax.

trigger_phrase: And taking up the matter, Iōb says,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If he should wish to enter judgment with him, he will not answer him one word out of thousand.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For he is wise in mind, mighty and great. Who, having hardened himself against him, endured?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: He who ages mountains, and they do not know, overthrowing them in anger.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: He who shakes what is under heaven from foundations, and its pillars totter.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: He who says to sun, and it does not rise, and seals up stars.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: He who stretched out heaven alone and walks as upon ground on sea.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: He who makes Pleiad and Evening Star and Bear and chambers of south.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: He who does great and unsearchable things, glorious and astonishing things without number.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If he pass over me, I will not see; if he go by me, I would not know.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If someone turn him away, who will turn him back? Or who will say to him, What have you done?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For he turned away wrath; under him sea-monsters beneath heaven were bowed down.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And if he should hear me, will he discern my words?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For even if I am righteous, he will not hear me; I will plead with my judge.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And if I call and he answers, I do not believe that he has heard my voice.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Let him not rub me out in storm-cloud; he made my shatterings many for nothing.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For he does not let me take breath, but filled me with bitterness.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If it is matter of strength, he is strong; but in judgment, who will withstand him?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Even if I am righteous, my mouth will act ungodly; if I am blameless, I will turn crooked.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For even if I did act ungodly, I do not know in my soul; only this, that my life is taken away.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Therefore I said, wrath destroys both great man and ruler.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For worthless men are remarkable in death, but the righteous are laughed to scorn.
footnote_text: Article cleanup: English supplies the for the righteous class-group subject.

trigger_phrase: For the earth is given into the hands of the ungodly; he covers faces of its judges. But if not he, who is it?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: My life is lighter than runner; they fled and did not know.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Or is there track of way for ships, or of eagle flying and seeking food?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If then I say, I will forget my speaking, stooping with face I will groan,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: I shudder in all my limbs, for I know that you will not leave me innocent.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Since I am ungodly, why then did I not die?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For if I wash myself with snow and cleanse my hands with purity,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: sufficiently you dipped me in filth, and my garment loathed me.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For you are not man like me, against whom I will answer, that we might come together into judgment.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If only there were mediator of us, and reprover, and one hearing between both.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Let him take his rod away from me, and let his fear not whirl me about.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Then I would not fear, but speak, for I do not know myself so.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Weary in my soul, groaning, I will let my words go upon him; I will speak bitterness of my soul while hard pressed.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And I will say to the Lord, Do not treat me as ungodly; teach me why you judged me thus.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Is it good to you if I act unjustly, that you reject works of your hands, but give heed to the counsel of the ungodly?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Do you look as mortal looks, or see as man sees?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Is your life human, or your years those of man,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: that you searched out my lawlessness and tracked down my sins?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For you know that I did not act ungodly, but there is none rescuing from your hands.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Your hands formed me and made me; then changing, you struck me.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Remember that you molded me like clay, and you turn me back into earth.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Did you not milk me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: With skin and flesh you clothed me, and with bones and sinews you wove me.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Life and mercy you set with me, and your oversight guarded my spirit.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Holding these things within yourself, I know that you can do all things, and nothing is impossible to you.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If I sin, you watch me, and from lawlessness you did not make me innocent.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If I am ungodly, woe to me; if I am righteous, I cannot lift myself up, for I am full of dishonor.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For I am hunted like a lion for slaughter, and again changing, you destroy me terribly.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Renewing my examination against me, you used great wrath toward me and brought trials upon me.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Why then did you bring me out from womb? Would that I had died and eye had not seen me.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And I would have become as if I had not been. Why then was I not carried from belly to grave?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Is not time of my life small? Let me be, that I may rest a little,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: before I go from where I will not return, into a dark and gloomy land,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: into the land of eternal darkness, where there is no light, nor seeing of life among mortals.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And taking up the matter, Sophar the Naamathite says,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Will one who says many things also answer back? Or does wordy man think himself righteous, blessed though born of woman and short-lived?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Do not become abundant in words, for there is no one answering you.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For do not say, I am pure in works and blameless before him.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: But how might the Lord speak to you and open his lips with you!
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Then he would declare to you power of wisdom, because they will be double to what is with you. And then you will know that what came to you from the Lord matches what you sinned.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Will you find track of the Lord, or reach to the ends of what Almighty made?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Heaven is high; what will you do? Deeper than things in Hades; what do you know?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Longer than measure of earth and broader than sea.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If he overturn all things, who will say to him, What did you do?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For he knows the works of lawless men, and seeing wrongs he will not overlook.
footnote_text: Article cleanup: English supplies the before works for readable object syntax.

trigger_phrase: But man drifts vainly in words, and mortal born of woman is like a desert donkey.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For if you set your heart pure and stretch out hands toward him,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: if any lawless thing is in your hands, put it far from you, and let not injustice lodge in your dwelling.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For then your face will shine like pure water, and you will strip off filth and by no means fear.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: How the faithful city Zion became a prostitute, full of judgment, in which righteousness slept, but now murderers.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Your silver is unapproved, your tavern-keepers mix wine with water.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Because a man will seize his brother or one of his father's household, saying, You have clothing, become our leader, and let my food be under you.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: He will answer and say in that day, I will not be your leader, for in my house there is neither bread nor clothing; I will not be the leader of this people.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: But now the Lord will stand for judgment and stand to judge his people.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: The Lord himself will come into judgment with the elders of his people and with their rulers: But you, why did you burn my vineyard, and the spoil of the poor in your houses?

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: It will be, instead of a sweet smell there will be dust, and instead of a belt you will bind with rope, and instead of the golden ornament of the head you will have baldness because of your works, and instead of a tunic bordered in purple you will gird yourself with sackcloth.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And it will be for shade from the heat and for shelter and hiding from harshness and rain.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And now, man of Judah and dwellers in Jerusalem, judge between me and my vineyard.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Woe to those joining house to house and bringing field near to field, to take something away from the neighbor; will you not dwell alone on the land?

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For ten yokes of oxen working will produce one jar, and one sowing six artabas will produce three measures.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Therefore my people became captive because they did not know the Lord, and a multitude became dead from famine and thirst of water.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.
