footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the beasts will rest there, and the houses will be filled with sound, and the sirens will rest there and demons will dance there.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And donkey-centaurs will dwell there, and hedgehogs will make nests in their houses. Quickly it comes and will not delay.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the Lord will have mercy on Jacob and will still choose Israel, and they will rest upon their land, and a resident alien will be added to them and added to the house of Jacob.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And nations will take them and bring them into their place, and they will inherit and multiply on the land of God as male slaves and female slaves, and they will capture those who captured them and rule those who ruled them.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And it will be in that day God will give you rest from your pain and your anger and your hard service with which you served them.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And you will take up this lament over the king of Babylon and say in that day: How the exactor has rested, and how the zealot has rested.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: God shattered the yoke of sinners, the yoke of rulers,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: striking a nation in wrath with an incurable blow, striking a nation with a stroke of anger from which he did not spare.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: All the earth rested confidently; it cries out with gladness.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the trees of Lebanon rejoiced over you, and the cedar of Lebanon: Since you have fallen asleep, the one cutting us down did not come up.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Hades below was embittered to meet you; all the giants who ruled the earth were raised up for you, who roused from their thrones all the kings of nations.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: All will answer and say to you, You too were taken as we were; among us you were reckoned.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And your glory came down into Hades, your much gladness; decay they will spread under you, and a worm is your covering.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: How the morning-star fell from heaven, the one rising in the morning; the one sent out toward all nations was crushed to the earth.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And you said in your mind, I will go up into heaven, above the stars of heaven I will place my throne; I will sit on a high mountain, on the high mountains toward the north.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: I will go up above the clouds; I will be like the Most High.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: But now you will go down into Hades and into the foundations of the earth.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Those seeing you will marvel over you and say, This man provoking the earth, shaking kings,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: placing the whole inhabited world desolate and pulling down the cities, did not release those in captivity.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: All the kings of nations slept in honor, each man in his own house.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: But you will be cast on the mountains as a loathed corpse with many dead pierced by swords, going down into Hades, as a garment soaked in blood will not be clean.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: So neither will you be clean, because you destroyed my land and killed my people; an evil seed will certainly not remain forever.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Prepare your children to be slaughtered for the sins of your father, so that they do not rise up and inherit the land and fill the land with cities.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And I will rise against them, says the Lord of hosts, and I will destroy from them their name and remnant and seed, thus says the Lord.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And I will make Babylon desolate for hedgehogs to dwell and it will be for nothing, and I will make it a muddy pit for destruction.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Thus says the Lord of hosts: As I have spoken, so it will be, and as I have counseled, so it remains,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: to destroy the Assyrians from my land, and from my mountains, and they will be for trampling, and their yoke will be removed from them and their glory removed from the shoulders.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: This counsel which the Lord has counseled over the whole inhabited world, and this uplifted hand over all nations of the inhabited world.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For what the Holy God has counseled, who will scatter? And the uplifted hand, who will turn back?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: In the year King Ahaz died this word came.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Do not rejoice, all you foreigners; for the yoke of the one striking you was broken, for from the seed of snakes offspring of asps will come out, and their offspring will come out as flying serpents.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the poor will be grazed through him, and poor men will rest in peace, but he will kill your seed with famine, and your remnant he will kill.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Howl, the gates of cities; let the cities cry out, all foreigners disturbed, because smoke from the north comes, and there is no one to be.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And what will the kings of nations answer? That the Lord founded Zion, and through him the humble of the people will be saved.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: The word against the Moabite land. By night the Moabite land is destroyed; by night the wall of the Moabite land is destroyed.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Grieve over yourselves, for Dibon is destroyed, where your altar is. There you will go up to weep over Nebo of Moab. Howl; on every head is baldness, all arms are cut.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: In her streets gird yourselves with sackcloths and lament on her housetops, and in her lanes all howl with weeping.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Because Heshbon cried out and Elealeh, as far as Jahaz their voice was heard; therefore the loins of Moab cry out; her soul will know.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: The heart of Moab cries within her, as far as Zoar, for a heifer is three years old. Upon the ascent of Luhith they will go up to you weeping; on the way of Horonaim they cry out, destruction and earthquake.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: The water of Nimrim will be desolate, and its grass will fail, for green grass will not exist.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Will it thus be saved? For I will bring upon the valley of Arabs, and they will take it.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For a cry joined the border of Moabite land, its howl as far as the well of Elim.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: The water of Rimmon will be filled with blood, for I will bring Arabs upon Rimmon, and I will take the seed of Moab and Ariel and the remnant of Admah.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: I will send as reptiles upon the land. Is not the rock a desert, the mountain of Zion?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For you will be as a flying bird, a chick taken away, daughters of Moab, and then lambs.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Counsel more; make a shelter of mourning for her always in noonday darkness. The fugitives are driven out; do not be taken away.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: The fugitives of Moab will dwell with you; they will be a shelter to you from the face of a pursuer, because your alliance was removed and the ruler perished, the one trampling on the earth.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And a throne will be set right with mercy, and one will sit upon it with truth in the tent of David, judging and seeking judgment and hastening righteousness.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: We heard the insolence of Moab, very insolent, his pride was dried up; not thus your oracle.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Not thus will Moab howl; for in the Moabite land all will howl. For the dwellers of Deseth you will meditate, and you will not be ashamed.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: The fields of Heshbon will mourn, the vine of Shebam. Swallowing the nations, you trampled its vines as far as Jaazer; do not join yourselves, wander in the wilderness. Those sent were abandoned, for they crossed the wilderness.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Because of this I will weep as the weeping of Jaazer for the vine of Shebam. Your trees Heshbon and Elealeh cast down, because over your harvest and your vintage I will trample, and all things will fall.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And gladness and rejoicing will be lifted from your vineyards, and in your vineyards they will certainly not rejoice, and they will certainly not tread wine into vats, for it has ceased.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Because of this my inward parts for Moab will sound like a lyre, and my insides like a wall which you renewed.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And it will be, when you are shamed, because Moab toiled upon the altars and enters into her handmade things to pray, he certainly will not be able to rescue himself.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: This word which the Lord spoke against Moab whenever he spoke.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And now I say: in three years, years of a hired worker, the glory of Moab will be dishonored in all the much wealth, and a remnant will be few and not honored.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: The word against Damascus: Behold, Damascus will be removed from cities and will be for falling.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: It is left forever as a bed of flocks and a resting place, and there will not be one pursuing.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And there will no longer be a fortress for Ephraim to flee into, and no longer a kingdom in Damascus, and the remnant of the Syrians will perish. For you are no better than the sons of Israel and their glory, thus says the Lord of hosts.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: It will be in that day, a fading of the glory of Jacob, and the fat things of his glory will be shaken.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And it will be as if someone gathers a standing harvest and reaps seed of ears of grain with his arm, and it will be as if someone gathers an ear in a firm ravine.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And stubble will be left in it, or as berries of an olive tree, two or three on a high tip, or four or five on their branches will be left, thus says the Lord God of Israel.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: In that day the man will be trusting in the one who made him, and his eyes will look to the Holy One of Israel.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And they certainly will not be trusting in altars, nor in the works of their hands which their fingers made, and they will not see their trees nor their abominations.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: In that day your cities will be abandoned as the Amorites and the Hivites abandoned from the face of the sons of Israel, and they will be desolate.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Because you abandoned God your savior and did not remember the Lord your helper. Therefore you will plant a faithless planting and faithless seed.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And on the day when you plant, you will go astray, and in the morning if you sow, it will blossom for a harvest; on the day he gives lot, and as a father of man gives lot to your sons.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Woe, a multitude of many nations; as the sea surges, so you will be troubled, and a rush of many nations will sound as water.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: As much water, so are many nations; as the force of much water rushing down, he will scare him away and chase him far, as dust of chaff of threshers before wind and as wheel-dust carried by a storm.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Toward evening there will be grief; before morning and it will not be. This is the portion of those plundering you and the inheritance of those inheriting you.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Woe, land of winged ships beyond the rivers of Ethiopia,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: sending hostages by sea and papyrus letters on the water. For light messengers will go to a lofty and strange nation, a difficult people. What is theirs beyond? A nation without hope and trampled, whose land the rivers now divide.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: All as an inhabited land will inhabit; their land will be inhabited as a signal lifted from a mountain, and as a trumpet's voice it will be heard.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Because thus the Lord said to me: Safety will be in my city as the light of noonday heat and as a cloud of dew in the day of harvest.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Before the harvest, when a blossom is finished and a sour grape blossoms into a budding flower, he will remove the little clusters with sickles, and he will remove and cut down the branches.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And he will leave them together to the birds of heaven and the beasts of the earth, and the birds of heaven will gather on them and all the beasts of the earth will come upon him.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: At that time gifts will be brought to the Lord of hosts from a people afflicted and plucked, and from a great people from now and forever, a nation hoping and trampled, which is in the region of the river of its land, to the place where the name of the Lord of hosts was invoked, Mount Zion.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: A vision of Egypt: Behold, the Lord sits on a swift cloud and will come into Egypt, and the handmade things of Egypt will be shaken from before him and their heart will be defeated within them.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the Egyptians will rise against Egyptians, and a man will war with his brother and a man with his neighbor, city against city and law against law.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the spirit of the Egyptians will be troubled within them, and I will scatter their counsel, and they will ask their gods and their carved images and those speaking from the earth and the ventriloquists.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And I will hand over Egypt into the hands of harsh lords, and harsh kings will rule them, thus says the Lord of hosts.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the Egyptians will drink water from the sea, and the river will fail and dry up.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the rivers will fail, and the channels of the river, and every collection of water will dry up, and every marsh of reed and papyrus.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the green rush, all around the river, and everything sown by the river will dry up, wind-blasted.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the fishermen will groan, and all casting a hook into the river will groan, and those throwing drag-nets and casting nets will mourn.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And shame will seize those working the split flax and those working the fine linen.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And those weaving them will be in pain, and all making beer will grieve and pain their souls.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the princes of Zoan will be fools, the wise counselors of the king; their counsel will be made foolish. How will you say to the king, We are sons of wise men, sons of ancient kings?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Where now are your wise men? Let them announce to you and tell what the Lord of hosts has counseled against Egypt.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: The princes of Zoan failed, and the princes of Memphis were exalted, and they will lead Egypt astray by tribes.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For the Lord mixed in them a spirit of wandering, and they led Egypt astray in all their works, as a drunk man and a vomiting man wander together.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And there will not be for the Egyptians a work which head and tail, beginning and end, will do.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: In that day the Egyptians will be as women, in fear and trembling from the face of the hand of the Lord of hosts which he himself lays upon them.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the land of the Jews will be a terror to the Egyptians; whoever names it to them, they will fear because of the counsel which the Lord has counseled against it.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: In that day there will be five cities in Egypt speaking the language of Canaan and swearing by the name of the Lord; one city will be called the City of Righteousness.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: In that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the land of the Egyptians and a pillar to the Lord by its border.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And it will be for a sign forever to the Lord in the land of Egypt, because they will cry to the Lord because of those afflicting them, and the Lord will send them a man who will save them; by judging he will save them.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the Lord will be known to the Egyptians, and the Egyptians will know the Lord in that day, and they will make sacrifices and vow vows to the Lord and pay them.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the Lord will strike the Egyptians with a great blow and heal them; he will heal, and they will turn to the Lord, and he will hear them and heal them.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: In that day there will be a way from Egypt to the Assyrians, and the Assyrians will enter Egypt and the Egyptians will go to the Assyrians, and the Egyptians will serve the Assyrians.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: In that day Israel will be third among the Assyrians and the Egyptians, blessed in the land
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: which the Lord of hosts blessed, saying, Blessed is my people in Egypt, and among the Assyrians, and my inheritance, Israel.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: In the year Tartan entered into Ashdod, when he was sent by Sargon king of the Assyrians, and he warred against Ashdod and captured it,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: then the Lord spoke to Isaiah, saying, Go and take the sackcloth off your waist and loosen the sandals from your feet. And he did so, walking naked and barefoot.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the Lord said, As Isaiah my servant has walked naked and barefoot for three years, so signs and wonders will be to the Egyptians and Ethiopians.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Because thus the king of the Assyrians will lead the captivity of Egypt and Ethiopians, young men and elders, naked and barefoot, with the shame of Egypt uncovered.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the Egyptians will be ashamed, defeated because of the Ethiopians on whom they were trusting; for the Egyptians were their glory.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the dwellers in this island will say, Look, we were trusting to flee to them for help, who were not able to be saved from the king of the Assyrians; and how shall we be saved?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: The vision of the wilderness: as a storm through a wilderness would pass through, coming from a fearful land.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: A hard vision was reported to me: a lawless one acts lawlessly, and an outlaw acts as an outlaw. Against me the Elamites and the envoys of the Persians come upon me. Now I will groan and comfort myself.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Because of this my loins were filled with weakness, and pains seized me as one giving birth. I did wrong not to hear; I hurried not to see.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: My heart wanders and lawlessness baptizes me; my soul has stood into fear.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Prepare the table; drink, eat. Rise up, rulers; prepare the shields.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Because thus the Lord said to me: Having gone, set a watchman for yourself, and what you see, report.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And I saw riders, two horsemen, a rider of a donkey and a rider of a camel. Listen with great listening.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And call Uriah to the lookout of the Lord. And he said, I stood continually by day, and on the camp I stood the whole night.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And look, he comes, a rider of a pair. And answering he said, Babylon has fallen, and all her carved images and handmade things have been shattered to the ground.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Hear, you left behind and you being pained; hear what the Lord of hosts, God of Israel, announced to us.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: The vision of Edom: To me one calls from Seir, Guard the ramparts.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: I guard the morning and the night. If you seek, seek, and dwell with me.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: In the forest at evening you will sleep, on the road, Dedan.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Bring water to the thirsty one; you dwelling in the land of Tema, meet the fugitives with bread,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: because of the multitude of fugitives and the multitude of wanderers and the multitude of sword and the multitude of stretched bows and the multitude of fallen in the war.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Because thus the Lord said to me: Yet one year, as a year of a hired worker, the glory of the sons of Kedar will fail.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the remnant of arrows of the mighty sons of Kedar will be few, because the Lord God of Israel spoke.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Night and day it will not be quenched forever, and its smoke will go up forever; for generations it will be desolated and for much time.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And birds and hedgehogs and ibises and ravens will dwell in it, and a measuring cord of desert will be cast upon it, and donkey-centaurs will dwell in it.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Its rulers will not exist, for its kings and its rulers and its grandees will be for destruction.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And thorny trees will spring up in their cities and in its fortresses, and it will be a camp of sirens and a courtyard of ostriches.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And demons will meet donkey-centaurs, and one will cry to another. There donkey-centaurs will rest, for they found rest for themselves.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: There a hedgehog nested and the earth kept her children in safety. There deer met and saw each other's faces.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: By number they passed, and one of them did not perish; one did not seek the other, because the Lord commanded them and his spirit gathered them.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And he himself will cast lots to them, and his hand divided to them to graze forever; you will inherit forever; through the generations of generations they will rest upon it.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Rejoice, thirsty wilderness; let the wilderness exult and bloom as a lily.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the deserts of the Jordan will blossom and exult, and the glory of Lebanon was given to it, and the honor of Carmel, and my people will see the glory of the Lord and the height of God.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Strengthen the loosened hands and disabled knees.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Comfort the faint-hearted in mind; be strong, do not fear. Behold, our God repays judgment and will himself repay; he will come and save us.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Then the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf will hear.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Then the lame one will leap as a deer and the tongue of stammerers will be clear, because water burst in the wilderness and a ravine in a thirsty land.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the dry place will be marshes, and in the thirsty land there will be a spring of water. There will be the joy of birds, a camp of reed and marsh.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: There will be a pure way, and it will be called a holy way, and an unclean one certainly will not pass there, nor will there be an unclean way there; but the scattered ones will walk on it and certainly will not wander.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And a lion will not be there, nor will any of the evil beasts come up upon it, nor certainly be found there, but redeemed ones will walk in it.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And those gathered for the Lord will return and come into Zion with gladness, and eternal gladness will be over their heads, for praise and exultation and gladness will seize them; pain and grief and groaning fled.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And it happened in the fourteenth year of the reign of Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians went up against the fortified cities of Judah and took them.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the king of the Assyrians sent Rabshakeh from Lachish into Jerusalem to King Hezekiah with a great force, and he stood by the conduit of the upper pool on the road of fuller's field.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Eliakim son of Hilkiah the steward went out to him, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Rabshakeh said to them, Say to Hezekiah, Thus says the great king, king of the Assyrians, In what are you trusting?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Is a battle-line made by counsel or words of lips? And now in what do you trust, that you disobey me?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Behold, you trust in this broken reed-rod, in Egypt. Whoever leans on it, it will enter his hand. Thus is Pharaoh king of Egypt and all those trusting on him.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: But if you say, We have trusted in the Lord our God—
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: now make a bargain with my lord, the king of the Assyrians, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you can give riders upon them.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And how can you turn away the face of one governor? The ones trusting in the Egyptians are slaves for horse and rider.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And now did we go up against this land without the Lord to war against it?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Eliakim and Shebna and Joah said to him, Speak to your servants in Syrian, for we hear, and do not speak to us in Judean. Why do you speak into the ears of the men on the wall?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Rabshakeh said to them, Was my lord not sent to speak these words to your lord or to you? Was it not rather to the men sitting on the wall, so that they may eat dung and drink urine with you together?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Rabshakeh stood and cried with a great voice in Judean and said, Hear the words of the great king, king of the Assyrians.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Thus says the king: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you with words that will not be able to rescue you.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And do not let Hezekiah say to you that God will rescue you and this city certainly will not be handed into the hand of the king of the Assyrians.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Do not hear Hezekiah. Thus says the king of the Assyrians: If you want to be blessed, come out to me and eat each one his vine and his figs and drink water of your cisterns,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: until I come and take you into a land like your land, a land of grain and wine and breads and vineyards.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, saying, Your God will rescue you. Did the gods of the nations each rescue its own land from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Where is the god of Hamath and Arpad, and where is the god of the city of Sepharvaim? Were they able to rescue Samaria from my hand?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Who of all the gods of these nations rescued its land from my hand, that the God of Jerusalem will rescue Jerusalem from my hand?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And they were silent, and no one answered him a word, because the king commanded no one to answer.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Eliakim son of Hilkiah the steward and Shebna the scribe of force and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah, tearing their tunics, and reported to him the words of Rabshakeh.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And it happened when King Hezekiah heard, he tore his garments and put on sackcloth and went up into the house of the Lord.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And he sent Eliakim the steward and Shebna the scribe and the elders of the priests clothed with sackcloths to Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And they said to him, Thus says Hezekiah: Today is a day of affliction and reproach and rebuke and anger, because labor came to one giving birth, but she has no strength to bear.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: May the Lord your God hear the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of the Assyrians sent to reproach the living God and to reproach the words which the Lord your God heard, and you will pray to the Lord your God concerning these remnants.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the servants of the king came to Isaiah.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Isaiah said to them, Thus you will say to your lord: Thus says the Lord, Do not fear from the words which you heard, with which the envoys of the king of the Assyrians reproached me.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Behold, I cast a spirit into him, and hearing a report he will turn back to his own land and fall by a sword in his own land.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Rabshakeh turned back and found the king besieging Libnah, and the king of the Assyrians heard that
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Tirhakah king of the Ethiopians went out to besiege him. And hearing, he turned back and sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Thus you will say to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your God, on whom you trust, deceive you, saying, Jerusalem certainly will not be handed into the hands of the king of the Assyrians.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Did you not hear what the kings of the Assyrians did to the whole earth, how they destroyed it?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Did the gods of the nations rescue them, whom my fathers destroyed, Gozan and Haran and Rezeph which are in the land of Theemath?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Where are the kings of Hamath and Arpad and the city of Sepharvaim, Hena, Ivvah?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Hezekiah took the book from the messengers and opened it before the Lord.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Hezekiah prayed to the Lord, saying,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Lord of hosts, God of Israel, the one sitting upon the cherubim, you alone are God of every kingdom of the inhabited world; you made heaven and earth.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Hear, Lord; look, Lord; and see the words which Sennacherib sent to reproach the living God.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For truly the kings of the Assyrians made the whole inhabited world and their land desolate
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: and threw their idols into the fire, for they were not gods but works of the hands of men, wood and stones, and they destroyed them.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: But you, Lord our God, save us from their hand so that every kingdom of the earth may know that you alone are God.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Isaiah son of Amoz was sent to Hezekiah and said to him, Thus says the Lord God of Israel: I heard what you prayed to me concerning Sennacherib king of the Assyrians.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: This is the word which God spoke concerning him: The virgin daughter Zion despised you and mocked you; at you the daughter Jerusalem shook her head.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Whom did you reproach and provoke? Against whom did you raise your voice and did not lift your eyes to height? Against the Holy One of Israel.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Because through envoys you reproached the Lord. For you said, In the multitude of my chariots I went up into the height of mountains and into the far parts of Lebanon, and I cut down the height of its cedar and the beauty of cypress and entered the height of a region of the forest.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And I set a bridge and made the waters desolate and every gathering of waters.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Did you not hear long ago what I did? From ancient days I arranged them. But now I displayed it to lay the nations waste in strongholds and the dwellers in fortified cities.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: I let go the hands and they dried up and became as dry grass upon housetops and as field-grass.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And now your resting and your going out and your coming in I know.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And your anger, with which you raged, and your bitterness came up to me, and I will put a hook into your nose and a bridle on your lips and turn you back by the way in which you came.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And this is the sign to you: Eat this year what you sowed, and in the second year the remnant, and in the third year sow and reap and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And those left in Judah will put forth a root down and make seed upward.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Because from Jerusalem the ones left will go out and the ones being saved from Mount Zion. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will do these things.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Because of this thus says the Lord concerning the king of the Assyrians: He certainly will not enter this city, nor certainly cast an arrow on it, nor certainly bring a shield against it, nor certainly circle a palisade around it.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: But by the way he came, by it he will turn back, thus says the Lord.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: I will shield over this city to save it for my sake and for David my servant.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the angel of the Lord went out and killed from the camp of the Assyrians one hundred eighty-five thousand, and rising early in the morning they found all the bodies dead.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the king of the Assyrians turned back and departed and dwelt in Nineveh.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And while he was bowing in the house of Nisroch his ancestral god, Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him with swords, but they escaped into Armenia, and Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And it happened at that time Hezekiah grew weak unto death, and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet came to him and said to him, Thus says the Lord: Arrange concerning your house, for you die and will not live.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall and prayed to the Lord,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: saying, Remember, Lord, how I walked before you with truth in a true heart, and I did the pleasing things before you. And Hezekiah wept with great weeping.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the word of the Lord came to Isaiah, saying,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Go and say to Hezekiah, Thus says the Lord God of David your father: I heard the voice of your prayer and saw your tears. Behold, I add fifteen years to your time,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: and from the hand of the king of the Assyrians I will save you and shield over this city.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And this is the sign to you from the Lord that God will do this word:
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: I will turn back the shadow of the stair-steps by which the sun went down, the ten steps of the house of your father; I will turn back the sun the ten steps. And the sun went up the ten steps by which the shadow had gone down.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: A prayer of Hezekiah king of Judah when he grew weak and rose from his weakness.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: I said, In the height of my days, in the gates of Hades I will leave the remaining years.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: I said, I will certainly no longer see the salvation of God on the earth; I will certainly no longer see a man.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: From my kin I left the remnant of my life; it went out and departed from me as one striking a tent. My spirit by me became as a weaver's web coming near to cut off; in that day I was handed over.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Until morning, as a lion, thus he crushed my bones. For from the day until the night I was handed over.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: As a swallow thus I will cry, and as a dove thus I will meditate, for my eyes failed from looking into the height of heaven, toward the Lord who delivered me.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And he took away the pain of my soul.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Lord, for concerning this it was announced to you, and you roused my breath, and having comforted, I lived.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For you chose my soul so it might not perish, and you threw all my sins behind me.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: For those in Hades will not praise you, nor will the dead bless you, nor will those in Hades hope in your mercy.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: The living ones will bless you, as also I; for from today I will make children who will announce your righteousness.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Lord of my salvation, and I will not stop blessing you with a psaltery all the days of my life before the house of God.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Isaiah said to Hezekiah, Take a cake of figs and rub and apply as poultice, and you will be healthy.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Hezekiah said, This is the sign that I will go up into the house of the Lord God.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: At that time Merodach son of Laadan, king of Babylon, sent letters and envoys and gifts to Hezekiah, for he heard that he grew weak unto death and rose.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Hezekiah rejoiced greatly over them and showed them the house of perfumes and myrrh and incenses and ointment and silver and gold and all the houses of the vessels of the treasury and all that was in his treasures, and there was nothing that Hezekiah did not show in his house.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, What do these men say, and from where did they come to you? And Hezekiah said, From a far land they came to me, from Babylon.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Isaiah said, What did they see in your house? And Hezekiah said, They saw all the things in my house, and there is nothing in my house which they did not see, and also the things in my treasures.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Isaiah said to him, Hear the word of the Lord of hosts.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and they will take all the things in your house and whatever your fathers gathered until this day into Babylon, and they certainly will not leave anything, but God said,
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: and from your children whom you begot they will take and make eunuchs in the house of the king of the Babylonians.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, The word of the Lord which he spoke is good. Let there be peace and righteousness in my days.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Comfort, comfort my people, says God.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Priests, speak to the heart of Jerusalem; comfort her, because her humiliation is filled, her sin is loosed, because she received from the hand of the Lord double her sins.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare the way of the Lord, make straight the paths of our God.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Every ravine will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be humbled, and all the crooked things will become straight, and the rough things into plains.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And the glory of the Lord will be seen, and all flesh will see the salvation of God, because the Lord spoke.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: The voice of one saying, Cry out. And I said, What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all the glory of man is as a flower of grass.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: The grass dried up and the flower fell,

trigger_phrase: but the word of our God remains forever.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Go up on a high mountain, the one bringing good news to Zion. Lift your voice with strength, the one bringing good news to Jerusalem. Lift up, do not fear; say to the cities of Judah, Behold your God.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Behold, the Lord comes with strength, and his arm with lordship; behold, his wage is with him and his work before him.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: As a shepherd he will shepherd his flock, and with his arm gather lambs and comfort those carrying in the womb.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Who measured the water with his hand and heaven with a span, and who set all the earth with a handful? Who set the mountains with a scale and the glens with a balance?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Who knew the mind of the Lord, and who became his counselor, who instructs him?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Or with whom did he take counsel and who instructed him? Or who showed him judgment? Or who showed him the way of understanding?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: If all the nations were reckoned as a drop from a bucket and as the tilt of scales, then as spit they will be reckoned.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Lebanon is not enough for burning, and all the four-footed animals are not enough for a whole burnt offering.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: And all the nations are as nothing and were reckoned into nothing.
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: To whom did you liken the Lord, and to what likeness did you liken him?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Did not a craftsman make an image, or a goldsmith having melted gold gilded it and construct a likeness?
footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

footnote_text: Brenton differs here. The translation follows the current fresh wording at this verse numbering point.

trigger_phrase: Did you utterly reject Judah, and did your soul depart from Zion? Why did you strike us and there is no healing for us? We waited for peace and there were no good things, for the time of healing and behold, disturbance.
